This is 060 turntable with a PAN on it instead of a plate: same place, same size, same whole 6-12 degree steps, turning CLOCKWISE, and on each third of the turn the filling changes - egg, bacon, sausages. The first crack was generated with the pan already at dish size and H3 leaned in 36%, which cannot be held: shrinking the frame to compensate leaves a 26% border of paper round it, and the pan grows past the frame edges so the measurement saturates and stops meaning anything. Regenerated instead with a SMALL pan (fill 0.58) and a locked-off camera, and it holds - 606 px wide on the first frame and 606 on the last. The whole clip is then zoomed by one fixed number, 1.483x, about the frame centre, which is where the pan body was placed when that first frame was built. No tracking, nothing to drift, and zooming IN crops so it can never expose an edge. THE SIZZLE IS QUICKER: full speed until the egg is down, then every third frame - it cooks in a third of the time and nothing is lost, because nothing moves in it but the bubbling.

168 frames exactly, so the shot runs 36.000 to 43.000 and lands on the song. 18 of transition, 45 for the egg going in, then five equal slots of 21: bacon in, bacon turning, sausages in, sausages turning, and the egg turn before them. BOTH REPORTS WERE RIGHT AND THE SAME CHANGE FIXES THEM. Chasing it cost sharpness: the rim measured 47.55 on the original photograph and 35.25 after the first polar round trip, which is the blur. Two corrections were tried and both failed - a per-angle radial rescale (claimed 0.51% but that was measured on the matte, not the visible rim) and an ellipse-to-circle affine, which made it slightly WORSE at 7.88%. So the outline is no longer corrected, it is REPLACED: the alpha is a drawn circle at a radius inside the true rim at every angle. The pan is perfectly round because a drawn circle is; the three spouts are gone because they fall outside it; and NOTHING IS RESAMPLED, so the photograph's own pixels are untouched and the blur does not happen at all. The handle is kept by taking the matte back outside the circle inside its own sector only. First attempt at that kept the spouts too - they stand 63 px proud and the threshold could not tell them from a handle that stands 297 px proud. MEASURED: the alpha is a circle to 1.5 px (0.468%, rasterisation) with exactly ONE protrusion, 33.6-49.6 deg, the handle. Sharpness back to the original's 47.55 rim and 23.63 handle. TWO FIXES. THE HAND IS THE FOREGROUND: the key returns a soft matte and soft anywhere inside a hand means the pan shows through it. Chasing the key's thresholds was never going to fix that - a hand is opaque, so the matte is made opaque: anything the key called half-hand becomes hand, holes inside the arm are filled, and the only softness left is a pixel at the outline. There was also a three-frame ramp at each end of the clip multiplying the whole arm down - six deliberately transparent frames, put there to hide a pop that cannot happen, since the clip's first frames have no arm in them at all. Part-transparent area went from 1.4% of frame to 0.4%, and what is left is the outline. THE HANDLE'S ROOT IS BUILT, NOT SMOOTHED. The grey-85 cut runs along a shaded casting so its boundary wanders, and every wander is a ridge. Blur-and-threshold at sigma 5 did not shift the lump (bigger than the blur) and raising sigma would have rounded off the hanging loop. First rebuild used a half-width about the handle's axis and left a step, because the casting is not symmetric about that axis. So the two edges are taken SEPARATELY, each drawn as a straight line from the real handle's own edge at D1 out to a wider foot at the rim - continuous at D1 by construction, straight all the way in, like the reference. Alpha still one protrusion; out of round off it 0.936%. Rotation unchanged: 0/60/120/180, 180.0 total, turns at 83/111/139 so the pan waits for the crack. The 43.85% roundness figure is the ARM crossing the measuring rays during the crack, not the pan; pan-alone frames read 1.24%.

THREE REPORTS, THREE CAUSES. (1) HANDS STILL SEE-THROUGH: hardening the matte could not put back what the key never found. The difference key drops pieces of hand wherever the hand matches what was behind it, so chunks of finger were MISSING, not transparent. Skin is the one thing in frame that is neither black iron nor white paper, so it is now detected directly and unioned into the matte. (2) THE EGG VANISHING FROM 63 TO 68 AND A NEW ONE APPEARING: ours was set to arrive six frames from the end of the clip, which left a gap after the engine's egg had gone. Ours now arrives the frame the yolk lands, and past that frame the engine's egg is not drawn at all - which also disposes of its malformed, flat-topped raw egg. First attempt cut the whole matte to skin from that frame and SHREDDED THE EGGSHELLS, which are still in shot between finger and thumb; the restriction is now confined to the patch of pan our egg occupies, so outside it hands and shells come through whole. (3) TIMELAPSE: browning a third at each rotation put the whole change on three frames and held still between them, which reads as the egg being swapped. It now goes raw to done continuously over 95 frames, quantised to a fortieth for the render cache. Rotation unchanged and re-verified: 0/60/120/180, 180.0 total, radius varies 0.50 px. The 43.83% roundness figure is the arm crossing the measuring rays, not the pan.

FOUR EQUAL QUARTERS. Turns on 42, 84, 126 - three rotations dividing 168 frames into four holds of 42. The first hold had been stretched to 83 only because the crack would not fit inside it, and the answer to that is a quicker crack, not a lopsided shot. The clip is resampled 73 -> 38 frames by picking evenly spaced source frames: nothing is cut from the middle of the action, it simply plays faster. The yolk lands on frame 31 and the hands are gone by 40, so the pan first turns on an empty stage. The build now warns if the performance does not fit rather than silently stretching the hold again. RAW UNTIL THE PAN TURNS. Cooking starts at the first rotation, not when the yolk lands - an egg browning over a still pan is not what the rotations are for. IT COOKS IN PLACE. Raw and cooked are two different photographs - different outline, different size, yolk in a different place - so cross-fading them was one egg turning into another. The raw still is now registered onto the cooked one first: scaled 0.951 by the square root of their area ratio so the whites match, then shifted +6 +17 px so the two YOLKS coincide, with the cooked pixels filling anywhere the raw does not reach so the blend cannot open a hole. After that the blend has nothing left to move. HANDS: skin thresholds widened (sat 22, value 45) because fingers inside the pan's shadow are darker and less saturated than fingers over paper, and a threshold tuned on the lit ones leaves holes in the shaded ones. Measured on the clip, the difference key returns ZERO on frames 0-7 and 62-72 - the arm entering and leaving - so those frames were always skin-only; mid-clip the union holds at about 450,000 px with no dropouts.

A RAW WHITE IS TRANSPARENT, and that is what makes it read as raw. Uncooked albumen is clear - on a black pan you see the iron through it - and it turns opaque as it sets.
